question.en: Do I Qualify for Medicare Extra Help (LIS) in New Jersey in 2026?
question.es: ¿Califico para la Ayuda Adicional de Medicare (LIS) en Nueva Jersey en 2026?

shortAnswer.en: Yes, if income is under $23,940 (single) or $32,460 (couple) in 2026.
shortAnswer.es: Sí, si sus ingresos son menores a $23,940 (soltero) o $32,460 (pareja) en 2026.

fullAnswer.en: Yes. New Jersey Medicare beneficiaries qualify for Extra Help in 2026 with income below 150% of the Federal Poverty Level, $23,940 for a single person or $32,460 for a married couple, and resources under $16,590 single or $33,100 married. New Jerseyans already enrolled in NJ FamilyCare or a Medicare Savings Program (QMB, SLMB, or QI) are deemed eligible automatically. Everyone else applies through Social Security or NJSave.
fullAnswer.es: Sí. Los beneficiarios de Medicare en Nueva Jersey califican para la Ayuda Adicional en 2026 con ingresos menores al 150% del Nivel Federal de Pobreza, $23,940 para una persona soltera o $32,460 para una pareja casada, y recursos menores a $16,590 soltero o $33,100 casado. Los residentes de Nueva Jersey ya inscritos en NJ FamilyCare o en un Programa de Ahorros de Medicare (QMB, SLMB o QI) son elegibles automáticamente. Todos los demás solicitan a través del Seguro Social o NJSave.

h1.en: Medicare Extra Help (LIS) and NJ FamilyCare in New Jersey (2026)
h1.es: Ayuda Adicional de Medicare (LIS) y NJ FamilyCare en Nueva Jersey (2026)

introParagraphs.en: New Jersey has more than 1.7 million Medicare beneficiaries, and a substantial share qualify for Extra Help, the federal Low-Income Subsidy (LIS) that pays most of the Part D premium, waives the deductible, and caps drug copays. The income and resource limits are set nationally by the Social Security Administration, but New Jersey residents have a distinct path into the program through NJ FamilyCare, the state's Medicaid agency, which automatically deems many low-income New Jerseyans eligible, and through New Jersey's own state-run PAAD and Senior Gold prescription assistance programs.
introParagraphs.es: Nueva Jersey tiene mas de 1.7 millones de beneficiarios de Medicare, y una parte sustancial califica para la Ayuda Adicional, el Subsidio Federal de Bajos Ingresos (LIS) que paga la mayor parte de la prima de la Parte D, elimina el deducible y limita los copagos de medicamentos. Los limites de ingresos y recursos los fija la Administracion del Seguro Social a nivel nacional, pero los residentes de Nueva Jersey tienen una via distinta hacia el programa a traves de NJ FamilyCare, la agencia estatal de Medicaid, que califica automaticamente a muchos residentes de bajos ingresos, y a traves de los propios programas estatales PAAD y Senior Gold.

introParagraphs.en: New Jersey residents will find the exact 2026 Extra Help income limits by household size below, along with how NJ FamilyCare enrollment or a Medicare Savings Program grants automatic eligibility, how PAAD and Senior Gold fit alongside Extra Help, and the step-by-step application process for those who need to apply directly. For income limits on New Jersey's Medicaid program itself, see [Medicaid income limits](/en/medicaid-income-limits). To check multiple programs at once, use the [Benefits Screener](/en/screener).
introParagraphs.es: Esta pagina detalla los limites exactos de ingresos de la Ayuda Adicional de 2026 por tamano de hogar, como la inscripcion en NJ FamilyCare o un Programa de Ahorros de Medicare otorga elegibilidad automatica, como PAAD y Senior Gold se relacionan con la Ayuda Adicional, y el proceso de solicitud paso a paso para los residentes de Nueva Jersey que necesitan solicitar directamente.

heading.en: Direct Answer for New Jersey Residents
heading.es: Respuesta Directa para Residentes de Nueva Jersey

paragraphs.en: Yes. New Jersey Medicare beneficiaries qualify for Extra Help in 2026 if household income is below 150% of the Federal Poverty Level ($23,940 single, $32,460 married) and countable resources stay under $16,590 single or $33,100 married. New Jerseyans on NJ FamilyCare or an NJ FamilyCare Medicare Savings Program are deemed eligible automatically, with no separate application required.
paragraphs.es: Sí. Los beneficiarios de Medicare en Nueva Jersey califican para la Ayuda Adicional en 2026 si el ingreso del hogar es menor al 150% del Nivel Federal de Pobreza ($23,940 soltero, $32,460 casado) y los recursos contables son menores a $16,590 soltero o $33,100 casado. Los residentes de Nueva Jersey inscritos en NJ FamilyCare o en un Programa de Ahorros de Medicare de NJ FamilyCare son elegibles automaticamente, sin necesidad de una solicitud separada.

heading.en: New Jersey Extra Help Income Limits by Household Size (2026)
heading.es: Limites de Ingresos de la Ayuda Adicional en Nueva Jersey por Tamano del Hogar (2026)

paragraphs.en: New Jersey uses the same nationwide Extra Help income thresholds that apply in all 48 contiguous states and D.C., since New Jersey is not Alaska or Hawaii (the two states with higher federal poverty guidelines). The table below shows the 2026 limits at 150% of the Federal Poverty Level for every household size, along with the monthly equivalent New Jersey applicants can compare against a pay stub or benefit statement.
paragraphs.es: Nueva Jersey usa los mismos umbrales de ingresos de la Ayuda Adicional a nivel nacional que aplican en los 48 estados contiguos y D.C., ya que Nueva Jersey no es Alaska ni Hawaii (los dos estados con pautas de pobreza federales mas altas). La tabla siguiente muestra los limites de 2026 al 150% del Nivel Federal de Pobreza para cada tamano de hogar.

heading.en: New Jersey Resource (Asset) Limits for Extra Help in 2026
heading.es: Limites de Recursos (Activos) para la Ayuda Adicional en Nueva Jersey en 2026

paragraphs.en: New Jersey applicants must also pass a resource test: countable assets below $16,590 for a single person or $33,100 for a married couple in 2026. Countable resources include checking and savings accounts, CDs, stocks, bonds, mutual funds, and IRA or 401(k) balances not yet in payout status. A New Jersey applicant's home, one vehicle, and personal belongings do not count toward the limit.
paragraphs.es: Los solicitantes en Nueva Jersey tambien deben pasar una prueba de recursos: activos contables por debajo de $16,590 para una persona soltera o $33,100 para una pareja casada en 2026. Los recursos contables incluyen cuentas corrientes y de ahorro, CD, acciones, bonos, fondos mutuos y saldos de IRA o 401(k) que no esten en fase de pago.

paragraphs.en: If a New Jersey applicant notifies Social Security of a burial set-aside, the resource limit rises to $18,090 single or $36,100 married, excluding up to $1,500 per person set aside for burial expenses from the countable total.
paragraphs.es: Si un solicitante en Nueva Jersey notifica al Seguro Social sobre una reserva para gastos funerarios, el limite de recursos sube a $18,090 soltero o $36,100 casado, excluyendo hasta $1,500 por persona reservados para gastos de entierro del total contable.

heading.en: NJ FamilyCare, Medicare Savings Programs, and Automatic Eligibility
heading.es: NJ FamilyCare, Programas de Ahorros de Medicare y Elegibilidad Automatica

paragraphs.en: NJ FamilyCare is New Jersey's Medicaid agency, and it plays a direct role in Extra Help eligibility, not just Medicaid coverage. New Jersey residents who have full NJ FamilyCare Medicaid coverage, receive Supplemental Security Income, or are enrolled in a Medicare Savings Program run through NJ FamilyCare (QMB, SLMB, or QI) are deemed eligible for Extra Help automatically. NJ FamilyCare sends the eligibility file to CMS, and no separate SSA application is needed for these New Jersey residents. In 2026, New Jersey's Medicare Savings Program income limits are $15,960 single or $21,640 married for QMB, $19,152 single or $25,968 married for SLMB, and $21,546 single or $29,214 married for QI, each with an asset limit of $9,950 single or $14,910 married.
paragraphs.es: NJ FamilyCare es la agencia de Medicaid de Nueva Jersey, y juega un papel directo en la elegibilidad para la Ayuda Adicional, no solo en la cobertura de Medicaid. Los residentes de Nueva Jersey que tienen cobertura completa de NJ FamilyCare, reciben Ingreso de Seguridad Suplementaria, o estan inscritos en un Programa de Ahorros de Medicare administrado por NJ FamilyCare (QMB, SLMB o QI) son elegibles automaticamente para la Ayuda Adicional. En 2026, los limites de ingresos del Programa de Ahorros de Medicare de Nueva Jersey son $15,960 soltero o $21,640 casado para QMB, $19,152 soltero o $25,968 casado para SLMB, y $21,546 soltero o $29,214 casado para QI, cada uno con un limite de activos de $9,950 soltero o $14,910 casado.

paragraphs.en: New Jersey expanded Medicaid under the ACA in January 2014, so low-income New Jersey adults under 138% FPL (138% of the Federal Poverty Level, $22,025 for an individual in 2026) generally qualify for NJ FamilyCare Medicaid, not just Extra Help. Because New Jersey expanded, the state does not have the ACA coverage gap that exists in the 10 non-expansion states (Alabama, Florida, Georgia, Kansas, Mississippi, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, Wisconsin, and Wyoming). Note that Extra Help uses a higher 150% FPL income test and counts gross income directly, unlike NJ FamilyCare and ACA marketplace subsidies, which use MAGI (Modified Adjusted Gross Income).
paragraphs.es: Nueva Jersey expandio Medicaid bajo el ACA en enero de 2014, por lo que los adultos de bajos ingresos en Nueva Jersey por debajo del 138% del Nivel Federal de Pobreza ($22,025 para un individuo en 2026) generalmente califican para Medicaid de NJ FamilyCare. Debido a que Nueva Jersey expandio, el estado no tiene la brecha de cobertura del ACA que existe en los 10 estados sin expansion. La Ayuda Adicional usa una prueba de ingresos mas alta del 150% del FPL y cuenta el ingreso bruto directamente, a diferencia de NJ FamilyCare y los subsidios del mercado del ACA, que usan MAGI.

heading.en: NJ PAAD and Senior Gold: State Help That Sits Alongside Extra Help
heading.es: PAAD y Senior Gold de NJ: Ayuda Estatal Junto a la Ayuda Adicional

paragraphs.en: New Jersey runs two of its own prescription assistance programs, PAAD (Pharmaceutical Assistance to the Aged and Disabled) and Senior Gold, for residents age 65 or older or ages 18 to 64 with Social Security Title II disability. These state programs have much higher income ceilings than federal Extra Help: PAAD covers New Jersey residents earning under $54,943 single or $62,390 married in 2026, and Senior Gold extends to $64,943 single or $72,390 married. Neither program has an asset test.
paragraphs.es: Nueva Jersey administra dos de sus propios programas de asistencia de recetas, PAAD (Asistencia Farmaceutica para Ancianos y Discapacitados) y Senior Gold, para residentes de 65 anos o mas o de 18 a 64 anos con discapacidad del Titulo II del Seguro Social. Estos programas estatales tienen limites de ingresos mucho mas altos que la Ayuda Adicional federal: PAAD cubre a residentes de Nueva Jersey que ganan menos de $54,943 soltero o $62,390 casado en 2026, y Senior Gold se extiende hasta $64,943 soltero o $72,390 casado. Ninguno de los dos programas tiene una prueba de activos.

paragraphs.en: PAAD and Senior Gold do not automatically enroll a New Jersey resident in Extra Help, and enrollment in one does not substitute for the other. Because Extra Help's income limit ($23,940 single) is much lower than PAAD's ($54,943 single), a New Jersey resident who qualifies for Extra Help almost always also qualifies for PAAD, but the reverse is not true. New Jersey residents in this lower income range should apply for both Extra Help (through Social Security or NJSave) and PAAD (through NJSave) to stack the federal Part D premium and deductible relief from Extra Help with PAAD's $5/$7 copay caps.
paragraphs.es: PAAD y Senior Gold no inscriben automaticamente a un residente de Nueva Jersey en la Ayuda Adicional, y la inscripcion en uno no sustituye al otro. Debido a que el limite de ingresos de la Ayuda Adicional ($23,940 soltero) es mucho mas bajo que el de PAAD ($54,943 soltero), un residente de Nueva Jersey que califica para la Ayuda Adicional casi siempre tambien califica para PAAD, pero lo contrario no es cierto. Los residentes de Nueva Jersey en este rango de ingresos mas bajo deben solicitar tanto la Ayuda Adicional (a traves del Seguro Social o NJSave) como PAAD (a traves de NJSave).

heading.en: How New Jersey Residents Apply for Extra Help
heading.es: Como Solicitan los Residentes de Nueva Jersey la Ayuda Adicional

paragraphs.en: New Jersey residents who are not already deemed eligible through NJ FamilyCare, SSI, or a Medicare Savings Program can apply for Extra Help through two channels: directly with Social Security, or through the state's joint benefits portal, NJSave, which screens for NJ FamilyCare Medicaid, Medicare Savings Programs, PAAD, Senior Gold, and Extra Help in one application.
paragraphs.es: Los residentes de Nueva Jersey que aun no son elegibles automaticamente a traves de NJ FamilyCare, SSI o un Programa de Ahorros de Medicare pueden solicitar la Ayuda Adicional a traves de dos canales: directamente con el Seguro Social, o a traves del portal conjunto de beneficios del estado, NJSave, que evalua NJ FamilyCare Medicaid, Programas de Ahorros de Medicare, PAAD, Senior Gold y la Ayuda Adicional en una sola solicitud.

heading.en: Common Reasons Extra Help Applications Get Denied in New Jersey
heading.es: Razones Comunes por las que se Niegan Solicitudes en Nueva Jersey

paragraphs.en: New Jersey applicants who apply directly through Social Security or NJSave are denied for a handful of predictable reasons, most of which can be corrected and resubmitted. Household income or countable resources over the limit are the two most common causes, followed by missing documentation of income or household composition.
paragraphs.es: Los solicitantes de Nueva Jersey que aplican directamente a traves del Seguro Social o NJSave son rechazados por razones predecibles, la mayoria corregibles y reenviables. Ingresos del hogar o recursos contables por encima del limite son las dos causas mas comunes, seguidas de documentacion faltante de ingresos o composicion del hogar.

heading.en: How to Appeal a Denial in New Jersey
heading.es: Como Apelar una Negacion en Nueva Jersey

paragraphs.en: A New Jersey applicant denied Extra Help by Social Security has 60 days to request reconsideration in writing, either by mail or at a local Social Security field office. If the denial came through NJ FamilyCare because the application was filed through NJSave, the applicant can request a fair hearing with the NJ Department of Human Services within a stated deadline, and free help is available from a County Office on Aging benefits counselor or the New Jersey State Health Insurance Assistance Program (SHIP).
paragraphs.es: Un solicitante de Nueva Jersey a quien se le niega la Ayuda Adicional por el Seguro Social tiene 60 dias para solicitar una reconsideracion por escrito, ya sea por correo o en una oficina local del Seguro Social. Si la negacion vino a traves de NJ FamilyCare porque la solicitud se presento por NJSave, el solicitante puede pedir una audiencia justa con el Departamento de Servicios Humanos de NJ, y hay ayuda gratuita disponible de un consejero de la Oficina del Condado sobre el Envejecimiento o del Programa Estatal de Asistencia de Seguro de Salud de Nueva Jersey (SHIP).

heading.en: NJ FamilyCare Context: New Jersey's Medicaid Agency
heading.es: Contexto de NJ FamilyCare: la Agencia de Medicaid de Nueva Jersey

paragraphs.en: NJ FamilyCare is administered by the New Jersey Department of Human Services, Division of Medical Assistance and Health Services, and today covers more than 2 million New Jersey residents, including low-income families, pregnant women, children, and adults under the ACA expansion group. For Medicare beneficiaries specifically, NJ FamilyCare also runs the state's Medicare Savings Programs, which pay Part B premiums and, for QMB enrollees, cost-sharing, and which double as an automatic gateway into Extra Help.
paragraphs.es: NJ FamilyCare es administrado por el Departamento de Servicios Humanos de Nueva Jersey, Division de Asistencia Medica y Servicios de Salud, y hoy cubre a mas de 2 millones de residentes de Nueva Jersey, incluidas familias de bajos ingresos, mujeres embarazadas, ninos y adultos bajo el grupo de expansion del ACA. Para los beneficiarios de Medicare especificamente, NJ FamilyCare tambien administra los Programas de Ahorros de Medicare del estado, que pagan las primas de la Parte B y, para los inscritos en QMB, el costo compartido.

en.question: What is the Extra Help income limit for a family of 4 in New Jersey in 2026?
en.answer: In 2026, a New Jersey household of 4 qualifies for Extra Help with income below $49,500 a year ($4,125 a month). This is the same nationwide limit used in every state except Alaska and Hawaii, since Extra Help thresholds are set federally by Social Security rather than by NJ FamilyCare.

en.question: What counts as income for Extra Help in New Jersey?
en.answer: Extra Help counts gross income before taxes, including Social Security benefits, wages, pensions, and rental income, with a few exclusions. This differs from MAGI (Modified Adjusted Gross Income), the calculation NJ FamilyCare Medicaid and ACA marketplace subsidies use, so a New Jersey resident's Extra Help eligibility and NJ FamilyCare eligibility can differ even at similar income levels.

en.question: What documents do New Jersey applicants need for Extra Help?
en.answer: New Jersey applicants need a Social Security number or Medicare card, recent tax returns or W-2s, bank and investment statements, proof of any other income, proof of New Jersey residency, and household composition documentation. Applying through NJSave can pull some records automatically, but income and asset statements are still required.

en.question: What happens if my Extra Help application is denied in New Jersey?
en.answer: A New Jersey applicant denied by Social Security has 60 days to request reconsideration in writing. If denied through NJ FamilyCare after applying via NJSave, the applicant can request a fair hearing with the NJ Department of Human Services. Free help is available from a New Jersey SHIP counselor or a County Office on Aging.

en.question: Can I work and still get Extra Help in New Jersey?
en.answer: Yes, working does not disqualify a New Jersey resident from Extra Help as long as total gross household income stays below the 2026 limit for the household size, $23,940 for one person or $32,460 for a couple. Wages are counted as income the same as Social Security or pension income.

en.question: Is New Jersey a Medicaid expansion state, and does that matter for Extra Help?
en.answer: Yes. New Jersey expanded Medicaid under the ACA in January 2014, covering adults up to 138% of the Federal Poverty Level ($22,025 for an individual in 2026). Because New Jersey expanded, there is no ACA coverage gap, and many NJ FamilyCare-eligible adults who later enroll in Medicare are deemed automatically eligible for Extra Help.

en.question: How long does the Extra Help application take for New Jersey residents?
en.answer: Social Security typically decides an Extra Help application within 30 to 60 days of receiving all required documents. Applications submitted through NJSave that also screen for NJ FamilyCare Medicaid can take a similar timeframe, since NJ FamilyCare coordinates its determination with the federal Extra Help decision.

en.question: What is the difference between NJ PAAD and Medicare Extra Help?
en.answer: PAAD is New Jersey's own state prescription assistance program with a much higher income ceiling ($54,943 single in 2026) and no asset test, while Extra Help is a federal program with a lower income limit ($23,940 single) and a resource test. A low-income New Jersey resident who qualifies for Extra Help should apply for both, since PAAD and Extra Help do not automatically enroll a person in the other program.

es.question: Cual es el limite de ingresos de la Ayuda Adicional para una familia de 4 en Nueva Jersey en 2026?
es.answer: En 2026, un hogar de Nueva Jersey de 4 personas califica para la Ayuda Adicional con ingresos menores a $49,500 al ano ($4,125 al mes). Este es el mismo limite nacional usado en todos los estados excepto Alaska y Hawaii.

es.question: Que cuenta como ingreso para la Ayuda Adicional en Nueva Jersey?
es.answer: La Ayuda Adicional cuenta el ingreso bruto antes de impuestos, incluidos los beneficios del Seguro Social, salarios, pensiones e ingresos por alquiler, con algunas exclusiones. Esto difiere del MAGI, el calculo que usan NJ FamilyCare Medicaid y los subsidios del mercado del ACA.

es.question: Que documentos necesitan los solicitantes de Nueva Jersey para la Ayuda Adicional?
es.answer: Los solicitantes de Nueva Jersey necesitan un numero de Seguro Social o tarjeta de Medicare, declaraciones de impuestos recientes o W-2, estados de cuenta bancarios y de inversion, prueba de otros ingresos, prueba de residencia en Nueva Jersey y documentacion de composicion del hogar.

es.question: Que pasa si se niega mi solicitud de Ayuda Adicional en Nueva Jersey?
es.answer: Un solicitante de Nueva Jersey a quien se le niega por el Seguro Social tiene 60 dias para solicitar una reconsideracion por escrito. Si la negacion vino de NJ FamilyCare despues de solicitar por NJSave, puede pedir una audiencia justa con el Departamento de Servicios Humanos de NJ.

es.question: Puedo trabajar y aun recibir la Ayuda Adicional en Nueva Jersey?
es.answer: Si, trabajar no descalifica a un residente de Nueva Jersey de la Ayuda Adicional siempre que el ingreso bruto total del hogar se mantenga por debajo del limite de 2026 para el tamano del hogar, $23,940 para una persona o $32,460 para una pareja.

es.question: Es Nueva Jersey un estado de expansion de Medicaid, y eso importa para la Ayuda Adicional?
es.answer: Si. Nueva Jersey expandio Medicaid bajo el ACA en enero de 2014, cubriendo a adultos hasta el 138% del Nivel Federal de Pobreza ($22,025 para un individuo en 2026). Debido a que Nueva Jersey expandio, no hay brecha de cobertura del ACA.

es.question: Cuanto tiempo toma la solicitud de Ayuda Adicional para los residentes de Nueva Jersey?
es.answer: El Seguro Social generalmente decide una solicitud de Ayuda Adicional dentro de 30 a 60 dias de recibir todos los documentos requeridos. Las solicitudes enviadas por NJSave que tambien evaluan Medicaid de NJ FamilyCare pueden tomar un tiempo similar.

es.question: Cual es la diferencia entre PAAD de NJ y la Ayuda Adicional de Medicare?
es.answer: PAAD es el propio programa estatal de asistencia de recetas de Nueva Jersey con un limite de ingresos mucho mas alto ($54,943 soltero en 2026) y sin prueba de activos, mientras que la Ayuda Adicional es un programa federal con un limite de ingresos mas bajo ($23,940 soltero) y una prueba de recursos.
